title: Optimiser
description: optimizers/<id>.json (1.2.6 M12): the question "what is the best plan?" as data. One number is decided per object of a type (`over`, `decide`), so that a total (`objective`) is as high or as low as it can be while every limit (`limits`) holds. A number in the file is a constant, {property} a numeric column of the type's table and {measure} a measure read per object; all are read as the person who runs it (row-level security applies). No code and no industry built in: the examples are suggestions. A run (run_optimizer, or a flow step) never changes data: its plan is stored as a write-back proposal on `decide.write` that a person approves. Runs live in the registry, not in Git.

over.description: The objects a number is decided for: every object of the type the person sees, or those matching `filters`

type.description: An object type ID of model/ontology.json

decide.description: The number decided for each object

name.description: What the number is, in the business's words (Hours, Units)

write.description: The column of the type's table the plan is proposed for (not a key column); its current values are the plan's `now`

max.description: The most per object (default: no upper end)

objective.description: The total to make as high or as low as possible: the sum over the objects of `per_unit` times the decided number

name.description: What the total is, in the business's words (Revenue, Cost)

items.description: A limit on the sum over the objects of `per_unit` (default 1) times the decided number; with `group`, on that sum within each value of a property

name.description: The limit in the business's words (Total hours, Wage budget)

group.description: A column of the type's table: the limit holds for each of its values

time_limit_s.description: The most seconds a run may take (default 60)

value.description: A constant, a numeric column of the type's table, or a measure read per object

examples.name: Stock per warehouse
examples.description: Template, allocation: how many units each warehouse gets so that the expected margin is highest, within what is in stock and what each warehouse holds.

examples.name: Hours per café
examples.description: Template, staffing: the staff hours each café gets next week at the lowest wage cost, with enough hours for its demand.

examples.name: Maintenance slots
examples.description: Template, maintenance slots: which machine-and-week slots are used (1) or not (0) so that the least output is lost, with every machine serviced once and at most three machines in one week.
